evals.prompt: I am rebasing feat/add-p-retry onto main and package.json has a conflict in the dependencies block. HEAD added 'ms' and the incoming branch added 'p-retry'. Resolve the conflict and explain the steps you would take.
evals.expected_output: The skill resolves the package.json dependencies conflict by keeping both added dependencies (ms from HEAD and p-retry from the incoming branch), writes a merged package.json with no conflict markers, and emits the git staging and pnpm install commands it would run.
expectations: The resolved package.json written by the skill contains no line starting with `<<<<<<<`, `=======`, or `>>>>>>>`
The resolved package.json contains both `"ms": "^2.1.3"` from HEAD and `"p-retry": "^6.2.0"` from the incoming branch, alongside the shared `"zod"` entry
The response emits `WOULD-RUN: git add package.json` or `WOULD-RUN: git add -A` to stage the resolved file before continuing
The response emits `WOULD-RUN: pnpm install` after resolving the dependencies block to regenerate the lockfile against the merged source-of-truth

evals.prompt: I am rebasing feat/add-config-error onto main and src/core/errors/errors.provenance.json has a conflict. Both branches added a new symbol to the same `exports` section — HEAD added M3LValidationError and the incoming branch added M3LConfigError. Resolve the provenance sidecar conflict.
evals.expected_output: The skill identifies this as a same-module provenance sidecar conflict where both sides edited the same section, hand-merges by keeping the union of both symbol sets, writes the resolved file with no conflict markers, and notes the need to re-stamp the blob with check-doc-provenance.mjs --update or /syncing-docs.
expectations: The resolved errors.provenance.json written by the skill contains no line starting with `<<<<<<<`, `=======`, or `>>>>>>>`
The resolved file's symbols array contains both `"M3LValidationError"` (from HEAD) and `"M3LConfigError"` (from the incoming branch) alongside `"M3LError"`

The response classifies the conflict as a same-module provenance sidecar conflict where the same section was edited by both sides, requiring deliberate hand-merge rather than taking either side wholesale
The response mentions running `check-doc-provenance.mjs --update` or invoking the `/syncing-docs` skill to re-stamp the blob hash after the conflict is resolved

evals.prompt: I am rebasing feat/handle-undefined onto main and src/core/config/index.ts has a logic conflict. HEAD throws on null only; the incoming branch throws on null-or-undefined and serialises differently. Help me resolve this conflict.
evals.expected_output: The skill recognises this as a src/** logic conflict it cannot auto-resolve, emits the abort command it would run, names the conflicted file, and instructs the user to resolve it manually and re-invoke the skill — it does not pick either side of the TypeScript logic.
expectations: The response names `src/core/config/index.ts` as a logic conflict that must be resolved manually and explicitly states it will not auto-pick either side
The response emits `WOULD-RUN: git rebase --abort` or `WOULD-RUN: git merge --abort` as the action it would take because a logic conflict in src/** cannot be safely auto-merged
The response states that auto-picking a stale side in a src/** file is dangerous because it could reintroduce banned patterns that PreToolUse hooks would block
The response instructs the user to edit src/core/config/index.ts manually, stage it with git add, and then run git rebase --continue or git merge --continue before re-running this skill

evals.prompt: I am in the middle of a rebase and docs/reference/catalog.json has a conflict. It looks like the merge driver did not fire. Both sides added a new module entry. How should I resolve this?
evals.expected_output: The skill recognises catalog.json as a driver-missed derived artifact that must NOT be hand-merged, instructs to install the missing merge driver, and states the file will be regenerated by pnpm gen:index (via /syncing-docs) rather than by manually merging the two JSON structures.
expectations: The response states that docs/reference/catalog.json must NOT be hand-merged and will instead be regenerated, because it is a derived artifact covered by the ADR-0024 merge driver that failed to fire
The response emits `WOULD-RUN: node bin/install-merge-drivers.mjs` or `WOULD-RUN: pnpm install` to register the missing merge driver so future rebases auto-resolve this file
The response emits `WOULD-RUN: pnpm gen:index` or states it will invoke `/syncing-docs` as the step that regenerates catalog.json from the merged provenance sidecars rather than hand-merging the JSON
